matchstick.title: Vertical sticks only in I, II, III, L
matchstick.principle: Only the numerals I, II, III, and L are built from vertical matchsticks; all other Roman numerals (V, X, C, D, M) consist solely of diagonal sticks, so vertical sticks cannot be taken from or added to them.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a move involves a vertical stick, restrict both source and destination tokens to I, II, III, or L.
matchstick.example: You cannot move a vertical stick from V to another numeral because V has no vertical sticks.

matchstick.title: Preserve token validity
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, both the token that lost a stick and the token that gained a stick must still form a valid Roman numeral or a permitted operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, check that each affected token remains a legal symbol.
matchstick.example: Removing the only vertical from I would leave an empty token, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Use numeric difference to guide moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of the left‑hand side and right‑hand side; the numeric gap indicates how much the total must increase or decrease, focusing the search on moves that adjust values by that amount.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, calculate the difference between the two sides to decide which numerals need to be increased or decreased.
matchstick.example: If LHS=7 and RHS=12, you need a net increase of 5 on the left or a net decrease of 5 on the right.

matchstick.title: I‑V order swap changes value by 2
matchstick.principle: Swapping the order of I and V within a numeral (IV ↔ VI) changes its value by exactly two (IV=4, VI=6).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric gap is a multiple of two and a numeral contains the substring IV or VI, consider swapping the order.
matchstick.example: Changing IV to VI adds 2 to the numeral’s value.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer between numerals
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick from a numeral that has at least two vertical sticks (II, III, L) to another numeral that can accept a vertical (I, II, III, L) decreases the source value by 1 and increases the destination value by 1, while keeping both tokens valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust two numerals by ±1 each and both contain vertical sticks, transfer a vertical from the larger to the smaller.
matchstick.example: Transfer a vertical from II (2) to I (1): II becomes I (value 1) and I becomes II (value 2).

matchstick.title: Never take sticks from V or X
matchstick.principle: V and X consist solely of diagonal sticks; removing any diagonal leaves an invalid shape (a single stick), so they must never be used as a source for a stick move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a candidate move would take a diagonal from V or X, discard it.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal from X would leave a lone diagonal, which is not a Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity
matchstick.principle: Operators may only be +, -, or = after a move; any other shape (e.g., a single diagonal, a three‑line symbol) is invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After moving a stick that touches an operator, verify that the resulting shape is still one of the allowed operators.
matchstick.example: Removing the only horizontal from '-' would leave no operator, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick from '+' to numeral
matchstick.principle: Moving the vertical component of a '+' operator to a numeral turns '+' into '-' (since it loses its vertical) and adds a vertical to the numeral, potentially increasing its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a '+' appears and you need an extra vertical stick, consider transferring its vertical part to a numeral.
matchstick.example: Transfer the vertical from '+' to I, turning '+' into '-' and I into II.

matchstick.title: Horizontal stick transfer between operators
matchstick.principle: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' (or vice versa) swaps the two operators: the source loses a horizontal (changing '='→'-' or '-'→'=') and the destination gains one (changing '-'→'=' or '='→'-').
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric gap suggests that changing subtraction to equality (or the reverse) could resolve the equation, consider swapping a horizontal between the two operators.
matchstick.example: Transfer a horizontal from '=' to '-' to turn "A = B - C" into "A - B = C".

matchstick.title: Reorient diagonal within V to create X
matchstick.principle: By relocating one diagonal stick of a V shape so that it crosses the other diagonal, the token changes from V (value 5) to X (value 10) without affecting any other token; this move preserves token validity and adjusts the numeral’s value by +5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a V appears in the equation and the numeric gap is exactly +5 (or –5), consider converting that V into an X by moving one of its diagonals to intersect the other.
matchstick.example: Turning the V in VII into X yields XII, changing 7 to 12 and satisfying "XII = XVIII - VI".

matchstick.description: Taking a stick from V or X, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be removed, forgetting that V and X consist only of diagonal sticks; removing one leaves a single diagonal, which is not a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never consider V or X as a source for a stick move; only take sticks from numerals that contain vertical sticks (I, II, III, L).

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid one
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may move a stick that destroys the shape of an operator, producing a symbol that is not +, -, or =.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move involving an operator, verify that the resulting shape is still one of the allowed operators.

matchstick.description: Assuming a single stick can change a numeral's value arbitrarily
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats any stick relocation as capable of any numeric change, ignoring the limited value adjustments each stick can cause.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Use the numeric difference heuristic and known value changes (e.g., vertical ±1, IV↔VI ±2, V↔X ±5) to evaluate whether a move can bridge the gap.

matchstick.description: Neglecting to recompute the arithmetic after the move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes proposes a move but does not verify that the resulting equation is numerically correct.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recalculate the integer values of both sides after a proposed move before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.description: Treating diagonal sticks as interchangeable with vertical sticks
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model confuses stick orientation, moving a diagonal where a vertical is required (or vice versa).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect the orientation constraints: vertical sticks can only be used in I, II, III, L; diagonal sticks only in V, X, etc.
